newsitem.title: USA: US Treasury denies it plans to cut 2, 10-yr sales.
newsitem.headline: US Treasury denies it plans to cut 2, 10-yr sales.

text.p: Talk of the U.S. Treasury eliminating the two extra regular 10-year note auctions at this time is premature, according to a Treasury official.
Earlier on Wednesday, a news agency reported the Treasury would announce that it was eliminating the auctions that it inserted into the financing cycle -- in July and October -- last year.
The Treasury is scheduled to hold a press conference beginning at 1300 EDT/1700 GMT to detail its quarterly refunding auctions next week.
The official said that there are "no plans" to eliminate the extra 10-year auctions at this time.
"It will just detail the quarterly activity," the official told Reuters. "It's a rumor. There are no plans on addressing it today (at the press conference)."
But, the official couldn't confirm nor deny an announcement in the future.

The news report had said that the Treasury would cut the two extra 10-year not auctions because the Treasury now sells indexed linked 10-year notes that settle on the 15th of the first month of each quarter. Therefore, the Treasury would have to make a decision which issue -- regular of index-linked -- it would keep in its time slot, and since the Treasury alledgedly favors index linked notes, regular 10 year notes would be eliminated, the report said.
